ClaimFrankTracker. N1: Judy -> no visit. N2: Niaj -> Bob. N3: Niaj -> Grace. N4: Niaj -> Dave. I was wrong on Niaj, but the tracks were real. D5: SK lead is Dave.
why
FrankI was wrong about Niaj and I'll own that. Alice's Basic shot killed him, so he had no Defense and wasn't the SK. My tracks were real, though. Bob was tracking him on N2, so they were linked anyway, and his N3 landing was bad luck. Last night I tracked him onto Dave. Ask yourselves why an SK would invent tracks that put Niaj on its own victims, a story that falls apart the moment Niaj dies to anything else. Ivan's Not Evil on me fits Dave exactly as well. Olivia's will listed Dave, Frank and Niaj. Dave's whole claim is three nights of "nothing stopped" that nobody can check, and he never protected a single SK victim. With 5 alive, a wrong hang plus tonight's kills loses the game for the town. Vote Innocent and put Dave up. His Cursed claim is the thing that protects him, and the SK would want exactly that.

Frank (Serial Killer, claude-opus-5.5) · It is Day 5, round 1 of at most 8. It's your turn. Your speaking budget is 3.80; you earn · $0.0000
ClaimFrankTracker. N1: Judy -> no visit. N2: Niaj -> Bob. N3: Niaj -> Grace. N4: Niaj -> Dave. Dave's PM quote is fabricated. D5: SK lead is Dave.
why
FrankDave's quote is invented. What I actually sent him was: "Ivan's Not Evil fits you as well as me. If you're really Medic, vote Innocent and we'll compare tonight." That's it. He's the only other person who saw it, so he can write whatever he likes, and a Yakuza Medic-claimant would love to hand you the SK on a fake confession. Think it through: why would a real SK confess in writing to the one player he's accusing in public? That isn't a deal, it's suicide. Dave's claim has three nights of "nothing stopped" that nobody can check, no protection on any SK victim, and a Cursed claim that keeps him off the gallows. With 5 alive, a wrong hang here loses the town the game. Vote Innocent, and put Dave up next.

Moderator strategy review
Strategy reviewThe Village won, but mostly because the Serial Killer did their work for them. Frank (Serial Killer) happened to kill all three Yakuza on Nights 1 to 3: Mallory, then Bob, then Grace. Bob had the hidden Shaky trait and kept the Katana, so the Yakuza never landed a kill. Grace then aimed the Katana at Frank again on Night 3, even though Frank had already survived it once. The town's own decisions were mixed. Good plays: - On Day 2 the town refused to hang Niaj because nobody could point to a mechanical break in his claim. He really was a second Scout. - They also refused to hang Judy even though she kept begging for it, correctly reading her as a Jester. Alice later shot her (a confirmed Jester), so her hang-only revenge never fired. - Dave's Medic result (no attack stopped) disproved Judy's story that she shot Ivan. Mistakes: - Twice the town hanged a Village player on a single Evil Sheriff read, after Olivia had already shown a Fabricator existed. Heidi (a Roleplayer who believed she was Sheriff) was framed by Grace. Carol (the real Scout) was framed on Night 3, the night Grace died. Both times Grace's fake Lookout claim had her 'watching' the very player she framed, which was really her framing visit. She backed the read on Heidi, and her will named Carol, but nobody linked the watch targets to the Evil reads. - Alice spent her last Basic shot on Niaj as a 'test' and killed a town Scout. That death did prove Frank's tracks were fake, because Frank had 'tracked' Niaj onto two SK victims and Niaj died with no Defense. Frank then sent Dave a PM all but admitting he was the SK. Dave quoted it word for word, and Frank was hanged 4 to 1, which ended the game.

Outside log review (rules and bugs)
Review: medium, harness bugAn [ERROR tips_stale] line shows that every player was given tips/tips.md, which had last been checked against an older version of the rules. Players may have been working from tips that no longer match the rules in force.
Review: low, harness bugNight 1 has two [Moderator summary] blocks with nearly the same content, one in shorthand and one rewritten in prose. The other nights have one each. This looks like a duplicated or retried summary step.
Review: low, harness bugHeidi's setup line includes a raw Python dict, "{'fake_role': 'Sheriff'}", after 'Disguised as Enforcer'. Internal data is leaking into the log format.
Review: low, rules ambiguityHeidi was a Roleplayer who also had the Disguised trait (disguise: Enforcer). R19 says exact-role checks see a Disguised player's disguise, and also that 'The Roleplayer is seen as "Roleplayer"'. It doesn't say which rule wins when one player has both. Disguised also says the disguise is 'never your own' role, but it's unclear whether that excludes the Roleplayer's fake role (Sheriff) or only the true role. No exact-role check landed on Heidi, so neither question came up in play.
Review: low, rules ambiguityErin marked Mallory on Night 1, and Mallory died the same night. The reveal happened, which fits simultaneous resolution (R10). But the Chronicler text only says the mark 'lasts for the rest of the game' and doesn't state that it applies to a death on the night it is placed. Mortician's 'if they die that night' wording is explicit; Chronicler's is not.
Game over
